quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Validation engineers design or plan protocols for equipment or processes so that products meet internal and external purity, safety and quality requirements.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Validation Engineers) include Validation Specialist, Product Quality Engineer, Supplier Quality Engineer and Quality Assurance Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a validation engineer does
paragraphs: Validation engineers design or plan protocols for equipment or processes so that products meet internal and external purity, safety and quality requirements.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Validation Engineers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Study product characteristics and customer requirements to set validation objectives and standards.
Write validation plans, process flow diagrams, test cases and standard operating procedures.
Run validation or qualification tests on new or existing processes, equipment or software.
Analyse test data to decide whether the criteria were met, or to find root causes.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering; B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering.
Less common routes on the map: B.Tech (Bachelor of Technology).
